headline: Cooper Investors initiated a key position in Deterra Royalties, attracted by the world-class MAC iron ore royalty following significant de-rating post Trident acquisition
reasoning: DRR was spun out of Iluka in 2020 and its primary asset is the Mining Area C (MAC) iron ore royalty, which underpins one of BHP's four large Pilbara iron ore hubs running at ~140 million dry metric tonnes per annum with a 50-year mine life disclosed by BHP. The MAC royalty is first-quartile on the cost curve and ranks among the highest quality royalties globally given its tier-1 operator and long duration. DRR significantly de-rated after acquiring UK-listed Trident Royalties and subsequently cutting its dividend payout to fund further acquisitions, creating Cooper Investors' entry opportunity. The concern is that reinvesting MAC's high-quality, fully franked cash flows into lower-returning, unfranked royalty assets risks being dilutionary and destroying value for DRR shareholders. Cooper Investors has been engaging with the Board and management to make this view clear. The fund classifies royalties under its Real Assets and Income Securities pool, viewing royalty income as higher quality than profit-based streams due to absence of operating and capex volatility.
quote: As mentioned above, our opportunity to buy DRR/MAC came after DRR acquired the UK listed Trident Royalties and the stock significantly de-rated over subsequent months... The de-rating of DRR is simple to understand. The MAC asset is a high-quality royalty and its cashflows, which had previously been streamed directly out of DRR to shareholders via fully franked dividends, are most valuable to shareholders that can fully utilise the franking credit. Investing this cashflow into risky, likely lower-returning royalty cash flows that don't have the ability to return franked dividends has a high chance of being dilutionary to MAC and destroying value for DRR shareholders. We have been engaging with the Board and management team to make our view clear.
episode_title: CI Brunswick Fund Annual Letter FY2025

headline: Sandon Capital views Deterra Royalties' MAC Royalty as the best asset in Australian mining, with strong fully franked dividends underpinned by BHP's South Flank ramp-up.
reasoning: DRR's primary asset is a royalty over BHP's Mining Area C iron ore operations in the Pilbara, providing direct revenue exposure without the risks of owning, developing or operating a mine. The counterparty risk is minimal given BHP is the world's largest mining company and MAC is one of the highest-margin iron ore mines globally. DRR has received over $450m in royalty and capacity payments from BHP in the past two years alone, passing these through as fully franked dividends under its 100% payout policy. When South Flank ramps to full capacity in CY24, total MAC production is expected to reach ~145Mwmtpa; even at a conservative US$80/t iron ore price assumption, annual royalty payments could approach $200m, equating to ~25cps of fully franked dividends, a ~5.5% yield on current share price. Sandon has low confidence in DRR's stated ambition to grow via acquiring additional royalties but expects strong cash flows and dividends from the MAC Royalty to continue.
quote: In our opinion, the MAC Royalty is the best asset in the Australian mining sector. The royalty provides direct exposure to the revenues of iron ore production from Mining Area C without the typical risks that are inherent in mining assets. DRR does not have to concern itself with permitting, exploration, financing, capital expenditure, mine construction, operating costs, mine and equipment repair and maintenance, rehabilitation and all of the other risks that come with the ownership, development, operation and closure of mining operations. The company simply collects a royalty cheque from BHP Billiton each quarter that Mining Area C produces iron ore. In the last two years alone, DRR has received in excess of $450m in royalty and capacity payments from BHP, bringing total payments since inception of the royalty in 2003 to ~A$1.4bn. These royalty payments have been passed through to shareholders (after deduction of tax and corporate costs) as fully franked dividends on account of DRR's 100% dividend payout ratio. DRR shareholders have received ~60cps of dividends over the past two years, and strong dividends look set to continue as a result of a strong iron ore price and further capacity payments.
episode_title: Sandon Capital Activist Fund Monthly Report Feb 23

headline: Sandon Capital sees Deterra Royalties worth north of $3bn (>$6/share) and retains it as a core holding following strong post-demerger performance.
reasoning: DRR's share price has performed strongly since demerging from Iluka, reaching a market cap exceeding $2.5bn. When Sandon first publicly campaigned for ILU to demerge the Mining Area C (MAC) royalty in November 2016, they valued it at $1.6-1.8bn based on 110Mtpa production and US$60/t iron ore. With MAC now expected to produce ~140Mtpa at full capacity and using a long-term iron ore price of $70/t (vs spot >US$140/t), Sandon believes the MAC royalty could be worth north of $3bn, implying a DRR share price above $6. DRR remains a core holding for the portfolio.
quote: Following the demerger from Iluka Ltd (ILU), the DRR share price has performed strongly with the company now having a market capitalisation in excess of $2.5bn. When we first went public with our campaign arguing for ILU to demerge its Mining Area C (MAC) royalty in November 2016, we valued the asset at $1.6-1.8bn. This was predicated on expanded MAC production of 110Mtpa and an iron ore price of US$60/t. Whilst our valuation was more than double the consensus broker valuations for the MAC royalty at the time, it is now apparent we were too conservative. With an expanded MAC now expected to produce ~140Mtpa at full capacity and using a long-term iron ore price of $70/t (vs spot at >US$140/t), we believe the MAC royalty could be worth north of $3bn (equating to a DRR share price >$6). Suffice it to say, the decision by the ILU Board to demerge the MAC royalty has been well and truly vindicated. DRR remains a core holding for the portfolio.
episode_title: Sandon Capital Activist Fund Monthly Report Nov 20
